proposals.before: Pingqiu included Linji Pavilion, where Tian Dan met his death, together with Kuang and Huangchi Pavilion.
proposals.after: Pingqiu had Linji Pavilion, where Tian Dan died.
proposals.reason: Chinese unit only mentions Linji Pavilion and Tian Dan’s death; Kuang and Huangchi belong to the following units.

proposals.before: Pingqiu: it had Linji pavilion, where Tian Dan died; it had Kuang; it had Huangchi pavilion.
proposals.after: Pingqiu: it had Linji pavilion, where Tian Dan died.
proposals.reason: Literal English fused the next two Chinese sentences about Kuang and Huangchi into this unit.

proposals.before: Yongqiu was the old state of Qi. The Chenliu zhi says, “Inside the city was a divine well that could bring forth fog and hail.” Xu Qimin’s Beizheng ji says, “It had Lü Lu’s Terrace, seven zhang high, and a shrine to Li Sheng.” Cao Zhi’s Praise of Yu’s Temple says, “There was a shrine to Yu, which Zhi moved into the city; the city was originally called Qi city.”
proposals.after: Yongqiu was originally the state of Qi (杞). The Chenliu zhi says, “Inside the city was a divine well that could bring forth fog and hail.” Xu Qimin’s Beizheng ji says, “It had Lü Lu’s Terrace, seven zhang high, and a shrine to Li Sheng.” Cao Zhi’s Praise of Yu’s Temple says, “There was a shrine to Yu, which Zhi moved into the city; the city was originally called Qi city.”
proposals.reason: Chinese 杞国 is the Si-surname state Qi/Ji, easily confused with Qi (齊) if left unmarked in English.

proposals.before: Changyuan was organized as a marquisate and contained the settlements of Kuang, Pu, and Ji.
proposals.reason: Chinese unit only states it was a marquisate; Kuang, Pu, and Ji cities belong to the following units.

proposals.before: Jiwu had Daji Township and Shou Township.
proposals.reason: Chinese mentions only Daji Township; Shou Township is the next unit.

proposals.before: Liaocheng held Yiyi Gathering and Nie city.
proposals.reason: Chinese mentions only Yiyi Gathering; Nie city is the following unit.

proposals.before: Leping was a marquisate once called Qing until Emperor Zhang altered the name.
proposals.reason: Chinese unit only says marquisate; the Qing rename by Emperor Zhang is the next unit.

proposals.before: Yangping was a marquisate with Shen Pavilion and Gangcheng city.
proposals.reason: Chinese unit only says marquisate; Shen Pavilion and Gangcheng are later units.

proposals.before: Liangfu was a marquisate with Tuqiu Gathering.
proposals.reason: Chinese unit only states marquisate; Tuqiu is the next unit.

proposals.before: It had Luqiu Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition says, “Shuqi of Zhu came over with Qi and Luqiu,” in Duke Xiang 21; Du Yu places Qi Township northeast of the county and Xianlu Pavilion northwest of it. For Duke Ai 7, when the viscount of Zhu, Fuxia, was imprisoned, Du Yu places Xiaqiu City northwest of the county.
proposals.after: It had Luqiu Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition says, “Shuqi of Zhu came over with Qi and Luqiu,” in Duke Xiang 21; Du Yu places Qi Township northeast of the county and Xianlu Pavilion northwest of it. For Duke Ai 7, when the Viscount of Zhu was imprisoned at Fuxia, Du Yu places Xiaqiu City northwest of the county.
proposals.reason: 負瑕 is the place of imprisonment, not the viscount’s personal name.

decisions.reason: Kuang, Pu, and Ji are separate following entries, not part of this marquisate sentence.
Shou Township belongs to the following unit and should not be duplicated here.
Nie city is a separate following entry and the proposed sentence matches this unit.
The renaming of Qing belongs to the next source unit.
Shen Pavilion and Gangcheng are separate following units.
Tuqiu Gathering belongs to the next source unit.
Fuxia is the place of imprisonment, not the personal name of the ruler of Zhu.
